name: Topoiyo
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source; 5 other works consulted do not discuss stress.
catalog_citation: Grimes, Charles E. & Barbara D. Grimes. 1987. Languages of South Sulawesi. Pacific Linguistics D-78. Canberra: Australian National University. 216 pp. Open access, ANU Open Research (hdl 1885/145413).
catalog_locator: Appendix E 'Comparative word lists', SYMBOLS, apostrophe entry, p.94; Topoiyo phonetic note p.97; Selayar antepenult note p.96; Topoiyo (TOP) rows of the 202-item word lists, e.g. p.99, p.105, p.109, p.117, p.143, p.193; Topoiyo survey entry pp.55-56 (no stress mention).
catalog_quote: p.94 (Appendix E, SYMBOLS, entry for the apostrophe): "Stress in South Sulawesi languages usually occurs on the penultimate syllable. In such cases it is not marked in the word lists. Where stress deviates from the normal pattern or where stress may be unclear due to double vocoids, etc., it is marked with an apostrophe preceding the stressed syllable." p.97: "Topoiyo. Besides a normal voiced alveolar flapped [ř], Topoiyo also exhibits a sound which, after eliminating several other possibilities, seems to be a simultaneous backed [ɡř]. ... Examples of the Topoiyo [ɡř] are: [la'uɡřoʔ] rattan, ['baɡřaʔ] wind, ['ɡřaa] blood" (on the page the g carries the 'backed' under-diacritic and r the flap hacek). Word-list rows, Topoiyo forms unmarked: p.99 "TOP puu taɓe lařiʔ"; p.109 "TOP laa kami jojoʔoʔ mataeʔoʔ" (same page: "SEK dia kami 'kitaa kulaʔ"); p.105 "TOP bubuŋa bace jonoʔ pae" (same page: SEK 'řeaa).

new_statements.rule_in_words: Survey-wide transcription convention: stress is penultimate and left unmarked unless it deviates; the Topoiyo wordlist (202 items, F. Dawson, Jan 1983) carries no deviation marks, and the only Topoiyo forms printed with explicit stress marks (p.96) are stressed on the penult. Hence Topoiyo is treated as a regular penultimate-stress language, by implication rather than by a Topoiyo-specific statement.
new_statements.exceptions: None for Topoiyo (contrast Selayar, for which antepenultimate exceptions are listed on the same page).
new_statements.domain_note: Isolated citation forms in a survey wordlist; the stress sentence is an areal generalisation over all languages surveyed in (then) South Sulawesi province, applied to Topoiyo data, not a dedicated description of Topoiyo prosody. The only grammar sketch (Nurhayati, Yamaguchi & Nakashima 2002, ELPR A3-009, Indonesian) could not be obtained and would supersede this.
new_statements.identity_note: Grimes & Grimes' Topoiyo (TOP) wordlist was collected January 1983 by F. Dawson (SIL) from Topoiyo speakers of Kecamatan Budong-Budong, Kabupaten Mamuju (now Topoyo District, Central Mamuju, West Sulawesi); same language as topo1243, no dialect division reported. Note the stress sentence is phrased for 'South Sulawesi languages' in the geographic sense of the survey (all languages of the then province), which includes Kaili-Pamona Topoiyo; it is not specific to the South Sulawesi genetic group.

sources.note: Appendix E p.94 states that stress in the surveyed South Sulawesi languages usually falls on the penultimate syllable and is left unmarked in the word lists, with deviations marked by an apostrophe; the Topoiyo rows carry no deviation marks (checked visually on pp.117, 143, 165, 191 where scanned suggested apostrophes -- all scanned artifacts), and the three Topoiyo forms cited with explicit stress marks on p.96 ([la'u(gh)ro?] 'rattan', ['ba(gh)ra?] 'wind', ['(gh)raa] 'blood') are all penultimate.
